questions.question: For TaVCrW, is the 12x12x12 supercell size sufficient for converged free energy perturbation calculations when using MTP, or does the smaller cell introduce a systematic error >0.5 meV/atom compared to a 16x16x16 cell?
questions.rationale: The paper reduced the supercell size due to MTP slowness, claiming convergence. If this reduction introduces significant error, the 20x speedup is at the cost of accuracy.
questions.decision_use: Decides whether to accept the current 12x12x12 cell for high-throughput screening or revert to larger cells for accuracy-critical applications.
answer_requirements: Compare free energy perturbation results for TaVCrW using 12x12x12 and 16x16x16 supercells with MTP to quantify the error difference.
evidence_spans: As applying MTP is much slower than using EAM, a relatively small but still converged supercell size of 12 × 12 × 12 (3456 atoms) is employed instead of a supercell size of 16 × 16 × 16 (8192 atoms) when using EAM.
The resulting energy difference between the free energy perturbation and the thermodynamic integration approach is only 0.5 meV/atom.
